changes.reason: neatlogs is a required partner. Right now there's only local Doctor output, and the README itself says no dashboard export is proven. This one step unlocks part of the 25-point partner score and turns the live (non-Antigravity) agent path into real evidence. It also provides the cost data that cfo.ai needs.

changes.acceptance_check: At least one live run log shows a model-proposed candidate failing verification, then rollback, a new candidate and a verified finish, with matching neatlogs spans. Each attempt has an Entire checkpoint ID recorded in state.json. The results table lists every fixture, including failures, with no benchmark framing.
changes.change: Show real, unscripted recovery. Add 3–5 fresh fixtures with different failure types, for example a wrong boundary, missing validation, a wrong branch, and one fixture deliberately built so a naive first fix fails hidden or edge-case checks. Run them live so that the model's own failed candidate triggers rollback and a retry. Make Entire part of the runtime loop as well: an Entire checkpoint per candidate, plus a Graph impact check before replace_source. Report per-fixture decisions, rollbacks and pass counts in one table.
changes.reason: Agent functionality is worth 30 points, and the rules require substantial autonomous work with recovery and verification. The only real run took four decisions with no failure, and the rollback story is scripted replay. Running Entire inside the agent, not just during development, also strengthens a required partner demonstration that is currently thin.

changes.reason: Build in public is worth 15 points, and the public repo plus the actual quote-post submission are required. Without them, no other score counts. These steps are time-sensitive (it's October 11 now), and no handle has been chosen yet.

review.verdict: This is a credible, honestly documented first milestone, but it can't be submitted yet. It has one real model run on one synthetic fixture, and that run went straight from inspect to finish. The only recovery evidence is the scripted replay. Several required items are missing: registration and check-in, an exported neatlogs dashboard trace, a real cfo.ai output, a public repo, a video of 3 minutes or less, build-in-public posts and the quote-post submission. Entire evidence is only a Graph search used during development. The README's honesty about these limits is a strength, but at this snapshot partner_usage, video and build_in_public would all score close to zero. Mandatory evidence should come first; after that, the biggest differentiator is real, unscripted model-driven recovery.

snapshot_correction: Both reviewers relied on stale pending-publication prose. The public repository was already verified; their signup handoff is superseded by user authorization and actual access limitations.
